e.etymology: Taken from the stage name of Puerto Rican reggaeton singer Jhayco, earlier billed as Jhay Cortez. He built it from Jhay plus the first letters of his surname Cortez.
namesakes: Jhayco (Puerto Rican reggaeton singer, formerly Jhay Cortez)

e.etymology: For girls a spelling of Jewel, the English word for a gem, from Old French jouel. As a male name it comes from the surname Jewell, a medieval form of the Breton saint's name Judicael, generous lord.

assoc.t: jewel, the word for a precious gem (same sound)

e.etymology: A spelling of Garrett, a surname from the medieval given names Gerard and Gerald, Germanic compounds of ger, spear, with hard, brave, or wald, rule. Garret has long been used in Ireland.

From the title of Saint Jeanne de Chantal, a 17th-century French baroness. Chantal is a place name from Old Occitan cantal, stone. It is often linked to French chanter, to sing, but that is not the source.
A short form of Valentine, Valerie, Valeria and related names, all from Latin valere, to be strong or healthy. It has been registered as a full name for both boys and girls.
namesakes: Val Kilmer (actor, Top Gun and Batman Forever)
Val Chmerkovskiy (Dancing with the Stars professional)

e.etymology: An American name that rose in the early 1970s with actor Demond Wilson of Sanford and Son. It follows the sound of Desmond and Raymond; Demond is also a rare surname.
namesakes: Demond Wilson (actor, Lamont on Sanford and Son)

e.etymology: A respelling of Kiara, which is used both as a form of Italian Chiara, bright or clear, and of Irish Ciara, dark-haired.
An African American coinage joining the prefix La- to Marcus, the Roman name usually linked to Mars, the god of war.
A phonetic spelling in the family of Cady, Kadie and Katie, most used in the United States in the 1980s. Kady and Cady are also English surnames.
Brought into American use around 1990 by actor Kadeem Hardison of A Different World. It is usually traced to Arabic, either khadim, servant, or qadim, ancient.
namesakes: Kadeem Hardison (actor, Dwayne Wayne on A Different World)

e.etymology: A short form of Catherine, from Greek Aikaterine. The origin of the Greek name is debated; its old association with katharos, pure, gave the name its traditional meaning.
A respelling of Corbin, an Anglo-Norman surname that began as a nickname from corb, crow, from Latin corvus.
A spelling of Khalil, Arabic for a close friend. Khalil Allah, friend of God, is the traditional title of Abraham in Islam.
A respelling of Dakota, the name of the Dakota people of the northern plains, which means friends or allies in their language. It is also the name of two US states.
A modern American respelling of Michael, from Hebrew Mikha'el, a rhetorical question meaning who is like God?

From Arabic rida, contentment or approval, especially God's good pleasure. It is a man's name in much of the Arab world; in the United States it is given mostly to girls, often in South Asian families.
The English weather word used as a name, and a spelling of Rainey, a surname from Irish O Raighne that goes back to the Old Norse name Rognvaldr.
A spelling of Arabic Asma, borne by Asma bint Abi Bakr, daughter of the first caliph and an early companion of Muhammad. It is usually explained as lofty or exalted.
From Hindi sohan, good-looking or charming, a word that goes back to Sanskrit shobhana, beautiful. It is used across northern India and Bangladesh.
From the Scottish surname taken from the city of Stirling, whose name may come from Old Irish words for stream and pool. It is often treated as a spelling of Sterling.
Covers two related Arabic names from the root h-m-d, praise: Hamid with a long i, praiseworthy, one of the names of God in Islam, and Hamid with a long a, one who praises.
The Ukrainian and Czech form of the old Slavic name Bogdan, made of bog, God, and dan, given. It was carried to the United States by Ukrainian families.
A Latin American form of Jamila, Arabic for beautiful, with the -eth ending common in Central America. It is used alongside Yamileth.
The Bosnian spelling of Leila, borrowed through Ottoman Turkish from Arabic Layla, night. In Bosnian the letter j is sounded like English y.
The initials D.J. written as a name. They usually stand for a first and middle name or for a junior, as in David Junior.
namesakes: D.J. Tanner (eldest daughter on Full House)
e.note: Written out, it reads as DJ, the word for a disc jockey.

e.etymology: Spanish paz, peace, from Latin pax, shortened from Maria de la Paz, a title of the Virgin Mary as Our Lady of Peace. A separate Hebrew name Paz means fine gold.
A spelling of Marilyn, a 20th-century English blend of Mary and the ending -lyn. This form is used mostly in Spanish-speaking families.
From an English surname taken from a place name, such as the village of Keston in Kent. The first part of the place name is unclear; the ending is the common English -ton.
From Sanskrit nitya, eternal or constant. The spelling with th is the usual South Indian way of writing the name in English.
A German name of Slavic form, usually explained as a pet form of Valeria, from Latin valere, to be strong. German immigrants brought it to the United States in the 19th century.
An Igbo name from Nigeria, made of chi, God or one's guardian spirit, so, to follow or accompany, and m, me. It is often understood as God is with me.
The Ukrainian and Russian form of Natalia, from Latin natalis, of birth, in the church phrase natale Domini, the birthday of the Lord, or Christmas.
